phalāsāva.meaning_2: desire for fruit; hope of reward; longing for results
phalāsāva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text phalāsāva = phalāsā + eva, metrically shortened. Subject of samijjhati.
phalāsāva.translation_1: one who hopes for the fruit succeeds.
phalāsāva.translation_2: 8. For those who do not hurry, their heart’s desire is fulfilled;

kākātī.meaning_2: Kākātī; name of a woman (wife of Venateyya); name of a city
kākātī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name found in the Jātaka verses. The variant readings kākavatī and kākāti show textual uncertainty; in sentence 1 it names a place, in sentence 2 a woman. Nominative singular in the text.
kākātī.example_1: Dūre ito hi kākavatī [kākātī (sī.), kākāti (syā. pī.)], yattha me nirato mano.
kākātī.translation_1: Far from here is Kakavati, where my mind is delighted.”
kākātī.example_2: ‘‘ Diṭṭhā mayā, samma puṇṇamukha, kākavatī [kākātī (sī.), kākāti (pī.)] nāma devī samuddamajjhe vasantī bhariyā venateyyassa naṭakuverena pāpamakāsi.
kākātī.translation_2: “I have seen, friend Punnamukha, the case of Kakati, the wife of Venateyya, who dwelt in the midst of the sea and yet sinned with Natakuvera.”

cīdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ci (nominative singular of the pronominal/interrogative stem kiṃ, 'who?') and idha ('here'); used as a relative in the verses: yo cīdha = 'whoever here'. Sometimes analysed as cī + idha, but ci is the standard form.
cīdha.translation_2: Who here accepts the truth after examination,

saṃviditvā.meaning_2: having known well; having understood; having considered
saṃviditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of saṃvidati. Occurs in verse with attani ('within himself').

māgamā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Prohibitive mā with the aorist 2nd singular agamā (of gacchati). In the verse it addresses Kuntinī: 'do not go'. Sometimes written mā gamā.

āmanta.meaning_2: farewell; addressing; taking leave (of); "I bid you farewell"
āmanta.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in the fixed phrase āmanta kho taṃ gacchāma/gacchāmi, a parting formula. Probably a shortening of āmantayitvā or an absolutive of āmanteti ('having addressed, having taken leave'), used idiomatically as an indeclinable; the PEU entry analyses it as ā + manta + tvā. Kept as indeclinable, not as a verb form.

dānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An emphatic temporal particle, often following an imperative or future verb; in these verses it means 'now, at this moment'. Sometimes alternating with idāni.

mavoca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ma (particle) + avoca (aorist of vadati, "said"). In the verse mavoca gāthā = "so said the verses".
mavoca.translation_2: The great seers spoke the verses of the holy life, meaningful and with pure phrasing.

sakkohamasmī.meaning_2: I am Sakka; Sakka am I
sakkohamasmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sakko ahaṃ asmi, the speaker naming himself as Sakka, lord of the thirty gods (tidasānaminda). Appears at the end of a verse line in the Jātaka.
sakkohamasmī.example_2: Ahañca te nāmadheyyaṃ vadāmi, sakkohamasmī tidasānamindo.
sakkohamasmī.translation_2: As for myself, my title I proclaim, / Sakka, the lord whom thirty gods obey.

atthasandassanī.meaning_2: showing the meaning; demonstrating the benefit; revealing the truth
atthasandassanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Jātaka Aṭṭhakathā, added to explain sandassanī as 'shedding light on the meaning'. Nominative singular feminine, agreeing with katā; the meaning of sandassanī here is doubtful ('instructive' or 'pointing to the meaning').
atthasandassanī.example_2: 89. Esā te upamā rāja, taṃ suṇohi arindama [atthasandassanī katā (pī.)];
atthasandassanī.translation_2: 89. This is a simile for you, O king, listen to it, subduer of enemies;

nisādetvā.meaning_2: having seated; having placed (on); having made sit
nisādetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of nisīdati (caus. nisādeti); variant spelling of nisīdetvā in the second verse. Used with ucchaṅge: 'having seated (me) on the lap'.
nisādetvā.translation_2: Having made my mind clear toward them, having seated them on a spread of leaves;

avekkhiya.meaning_2: having looked at; having examined; having considered
avekkhiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of avekkhati, used in the text twice with the sense 'having considered for oneself'; the form avekkhiya is an -iya absolutive.

kannappakannaṃ.meaning_2: shifting here and there; ever-changing; (lit.) ear and reverse-ear
kannappakannaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in the simile kannappakannaṃ yathā rukkhachāyā, describing something unstable like tree shade. The PEU suggests kannappakanṇa 'constantly inhaling and exhaling'; the text's single -n- may be a variant. Used adverbially in the verse.
kannappakannaṃ.example_2: 4. Thīnañhi cittaṃ yathā vānarassa, kannappakannaṃ yathā rukkhachāyā;
kannappakannaṃ.translation_2: For the mind of women is like that of a monkey, like the shade of a tree that shifts hither and thither;

menaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] menaṃ is most likely me + naṃ (enaṃ), the emphatic/demonstrative particle naṃ attached to the pronoun me; some analyse it as na + imaṃ. In the verses it refers to the horse that is being led on with soft words. The PEU entries medhā and megha are unrelated.

dubbidu.meaning_2: difficult to know; hard to understand
dubbidu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse tesaṃ have dubbidu sabbabhāvo, dubbidu agrees with sabbabhāvo. The reading dubbidu may be a metrical or dialectal variant of dubbidū (du + vidū), and the commentary's variant saccabhāvo suggests some uncertainty. Confirmed as an adjective; not the homonym dubbidha ("of two kinds").
dubbidu.example_2: Ete naro niccayato [niccayatto (sī. pī.)] bhajetha, tesaṃ have dubbidu sabbabhāvo [saccabhāvo (syā.)].
dubbidu.translation_2: A person should follow these with caution, for their true nature is indeed hard to know.

etitthiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of etā (nominative plural feminine of eta) and itthiyo (nominative plural of itthī). In the text the following pañca agrees with itthiyo. Sometimes written as etā itthiyo.

nosi.meaning_2: you are not; you are not
nosi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of no (not) + asi (you are). Written nosi; alternative analysis no + si. Occurs three times in the verses.
nosi.example_2: tvaṃ nosi rājā bhava me sukhāya”.

upāramāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular present in the text (upāramāmi), so the ending is -mi, not -ti. The meaning is 'I refrain / abstain'.
upāramāmi.example_2: 92. Esāhamajjeva upāramāmi, na cāpihaṃ [na cāpahaṃ (sī. pī.)] kiñci kareyya pāpaṃ;
upāramāmi.translation_2: I will refrain this very day, and I would not do any evil;

sannipātayi.meaning_2: causes to assemble; brings together; collects
sannipātayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative. The text form sannipātayi is a shortened aorist (or eastern aorist) 3rd singular used in verse; the present stem is sannipātaya-. PEU lists it as kā,kri 'he caused to gather'. Could also be read as aorist of sannipātayati.

yamuddhariṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of uddharati, with the sandhi form yamuddhariṃ = yaṃ + uddhariṃ. The text is verse, so the form is used for rhythm.

makā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (sī. pī.) for akāsi in these verses; 3rd singular aorist of karoti. In pada 1 the subject is vihaṅgamo, in pada 2 mā ... makāsi is prohibitive.
makā.translation_1: It is too difficult to do, the work the bird did for the egg-born;
makā.example_2: Mā me paripanthamakāsi [makā (sī. pī.)], saggaṃ mama patthayānassa ’’.
makā.translation_2: Do not cause an obstacle for me, aspiring for heaven.”

evaṃkaro.meaning_2: one who acts thus; doing like this; acting in this way
evaṃkaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text evaṃkaro is nominative singular masculine, used substantively of a person (brāhmaṇo, samaṇo, macco).
evaṃkaro.example_1: Evaṃkaro brāhmaṇo hoti khemī, dhamme ṭhitaṃ tena amāpayiṃsu.
evaṃkaro.translation_1: One who does this is a brahmin and is peaceful; they said he is firm in Dhamma.
evaṃkaro.example_2: Samaṇo caraṃ hitvā mamāyitāni, evaṃkaro saggamupeti ṭhānaṃ.
evaṃkaro.translation_2: A samaṇa, conducting himself having abandoned attachments, one who acts thus achieves the heavenly mansion.

cāhametamicchāmi.grammar: sandhi, ind + pron + pron + pron + pr
cāhametamicchāmi.meaning_2: and I do not desire this
cāhametamicchāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ca + ahaṃ + etaṃ + na + icchāmi (na + icchāmi contracted to micchāmi with sandhi). Found in Jātaka verse 213.
cāhametamicchāmi.translation_2: 213. 'I do not desire this which comes from a gift from another;

byasanno.meaning_2: sinking; sinking down; sunk; despairing; despondent
byasanno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of visīdati (via sandhi vi + asanna). In the verses it describes one sunk or stuck in mud and in the mire of sensual desire. Nominative singular.

nīdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form nīdha occurs in Jātaka verse, apparently as an indeclinable meaning 'here' or 'now'. Its analysis is uncertain; it may be a sandhi or a rare particle. The related PEU entry nīgha is different.

visīlaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, agreeing with the noun it qualifies. Negated adjective of sīla.
visīlaṃ.example_2: Sīlavantaṃ visīlaṃ vā, vasaṃ tasseva gacchati.
visīlaṃ.translation_2: Whether virtuous or without virtue—one comes under his sway.

nopaseveyya.meaning_2: should not associate (with); should not keep company (with)
nopaseveyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] na + upaseveyya (optative of upasevati, √sev). Sandhi of na + u- as no-.
nopaseveyya.translation_2: The learned one should not associate with the bad, but should associate with the good;

māgacchi.meaning_2: do not go; did not go; not approach
māgacchi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] For mā agacchi: mā (prohibitive particle) + agacchi (aorist 2nd/3rd singular of gacchati). In the verses it seems to mean 'came' or 'approached', so the negative mā may be questionable.
māgacchi.example_2: 244. Kathaṃ nvayaṃ balaviriyūpapanno, hatthatta [hatthattha (sī. syā. pī.)] māgacchi vanibbakassa;
māgacchi.translation_2: “How could such a starveling wight catch a creature full of might?

tvevahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tu (but) + eva (indeed) + ahaṃ (I). Always followed by na ... bhaṇeyyaṃ in these verses: 'but I would not indeed speak a lie'.
tvevahaṃ.example_2: Sabbā ca najjo paṭisotaṃ vajeyyuṃ, na tvevahaṃ rāja musā bhaṇeyyaṃ.
tvevahaṃ.translation_2: Flow upstream the running rivers, I, O King! could never lie.”

saṃhīro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the verse. Probably from saṃ + √har (carry away), i.e. 'carried away by' (cāmisena). PEU gives 'deceitful; easily deceived'.
saṃhīro.example_2: Yo cāmisena saṃhīro, hadayattheno ca yo naro.
saṃhīro.translation_2: Or to one who is swayed by material gain, or to a person who is a thief of hearts.

sambodhayati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular present of the causative of sambujjhati, used here in the sense 'makes known, reveals'. The root is √budh (know, wake up).
sambodhayati.translation_2: The person who reveals a secret matter that was not understood;

tāvanto.meaning_2: so many; of that extent; as many
tāvanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular masculine in the text, agreeing with ubbegā. Same formation as yāvant and etāvant.

supariṇāmavā.meaning_2: well rounded; fully developed; well matured
supariṇāmavā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading supariṇāmavā for supariṇāhavā ('well rounded'). Possessive suffix -vant with -nt dropped before the nominative ending. Describes a pitcher in the simile.
supariṇāmavā.translation_1: 2. Like a great water-bearing pitcher, fully rounded,

ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhīva.grammar: sandhi, adj + adj + adj + adj + ind
ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhīva.meaning_2: like one smeared with a silver plate; as if touched with a silver plaque
ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhīva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhī (adj) + iva; in the text it describes a tigress (byagghī iva). The spelling ruppapaṭṭapalimaṭṭhīva (syā.) and rūpapaṭṭapamaṭṭhīva (ka.) are variants; ruppa = silver. The word is an adjective describing one polished or smeared (palimaṭṭha) with silver plates.
ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhīva.translation_1: 9. Like one polished with a silver plate, like a tigress born on the mountain slope,

rūpapaṭṭapamaṭṭhīva.meaning_2: as if pressed with a beautiful plate; as if burnished with a lovely slab
rūpapaṭṭapamaṭṭhīva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading ruppapaṭṭapalimaṭṭhīva is preferred by the editors; doubt whether the first member is rūpa (beautiful) or ruppa (silver). -iva is sandhi of iva.
rūpapaṭṭapamaṭṭhīva.translation_1: 9. Like one polished with a silver plate, like a tigress born on the mountain slope,

ambuni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (ambuni = ambu + ni). Related adjectives ambuda and ambuja suggest ambu means water.
ambuni.example_2: 15. Yaṃ kiñci ubhato tīre, phalaṃ patati ambuni;
ambuni.translation_2: 15. Whatever fruit falls into the water on either bank,

mabhisaṅgaṃ.meaning_2: do not indulge in attachment; do not delight in clinging
mabhisaṅgaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mā + abhisaṅga (masc, 'attachment; clinging'). The word is mā + abhisaṅgaṃ in the text. The comment in the second sentence may translate abhisaṅga differently.
mabhisaṅgaṃ.translation_2: Do not indulge in longing, restrain yourself, lord of generations.

āceyyamāno.meaning_2: being desired; being sought after; being wished for
āceyyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Rare causative passive present participle from √ci 1 (gather; note, observe) with the -eyya- sign; the reading and analysis are uncertain. Vocative usage in the text, modifying rājisi.
āceyyamāno.translation_2: Royal sage, you who desire death while being one who should be honored.

cīyatī.meaning_2: is accumulated; accumulates; is heaped up
cīyatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of cināti; the text has cīyatī before tassa, a sandhi form of cīyati. Also explained in PEU as 'increases'.
cīyatī.example_2: Na cīyatī tassa narassa pāpaṃ, sace na ceteti vadhāya tassa.
cīyatī.translation_2: Bad kamma is not accumulated for that person, if he does not intend harm for that.

isipūgasamaññāte.meaning_2: known as the company of sages; designated as the assembly of hermits
isipūgasamaññāte.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of isi + pūga + samaññāta (pp of samaññāti). Locative singular in the verse.
isipūgasamaññāte.example_2: 20. Isipūgasamaññāte, evaṃ lokyā viditā sati [pati (ka. syā. ka.)];
isipūgasamaññāte.translation_2: 20. Known among the assembly of sages, thus mindfulness is known in the world;

upānayāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular upānayāmi in the text; the related PEU entry gives upānayati as the 3rd singular.
upānayāmi.translation_2: I will lead you to a cool place, abide there without care.

pabodhare.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural present of the causative pabodheti (pa + budh + *e), with the ending -are for -enti. The text's pabodhare is a metrical or script variant; the sense is 'cuckoos awaken (the grove)'.
pabodhare.translation_2: Resound with flocks of swans, and cuckoos awaken [the grove] here.

kosumbhasalalā.meaning_2: kosiya flower; sesamum flower; name of a flowering tree or creeper used in garlands
kosumbhasalalā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a dvanda compound of kosumba and salalā rather than a feminine a-stem headword. The text is a list of plants, with nīpa and the ripe tāla palms; kosumba is the kosiya or sesamum flower, salalā is uncertain. Spelling saḷalā in the Burmese and Siamese editions.
kosumbhasalalā.translation_1: Kosamba, śalala, nīpa, and ripe palms hang down.

tiriṭī.meaning_2: wearing a wreath (of flowers); adorned with a garland
tiriṭī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive compound in a list of ornaments; nominative singular in the verse. PEU gives tiriṭa as a small tree and tiriṭi as cicada, but the context suggests a floral ornament.
tiriṭī.translation_2: 28. Wearing garlands, wreaths, armlets, adorned with sandalwood,

aṅgadī.meaning_2: wearing an armlet; adorned with an armlet
aṅgadī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a person wearing aṅgadas. In these verses it is nominative singular, parallel with mālī, tiriṭī and kāyūrī.
aṅgadī.translation_2: 28. Wearing garlands, wreaths, armlets, adorned with sandalwood,

candanassado.meaning_2: scented with sandalwood; having the fragrance of sandalwood
candanassado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading candanussada is given in the text. Nominative singular qualifying a king; a bahubbīhi compound describing the fragrance of sandalwood on the body.
candanassado.translation_1: 28. Wearing garlands, wreaths, armlets, adorned with sandalwood,

tiṭṭhasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular of tiṭṭhati; here paired with gacchasi, 'you go and stand'.
tiṭṭhasī.example_2: 34. So chinnavātaṃ kamasī aghamhi, vehāyasaṃ gacchasi tiṭṭhasī ca;
tiṭṭhasī.translation_2: Thou movest through the air, thou walkest there, and standest too.

dārukaṭallakova.meaning_2: wooden puppet; wooden figure; mechanical figure
dārukaṭallakova.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is dārukaṭallakova, i.e. dārukaṭallako + iva (like, as), in the nominative singular, used in a simile: 'so naccatī dārukaṭallakova' = 'he dances like a wooden puppet'.
dārukaṭallakova.example_2: So naccatī dārukaṭallakova, tassā puṇṇaṃ kumbhamimaṃ kiṇātha.
dārukaṭallakova.translation_2: One dances like a wooden puppet; buy this jar filled with that!

kalahāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural form in the verse (kalahāni). Alternatively could be read as adjective kalahin (quarrelsome), but the PEU and commentary support the neuter plural noun kalahāni. The root √kal 1 (spend time, disturb) is uncertain; some derive from √kalah (argue).
kalahāni.example_2: 44. Mānātimānā kalahāni pesuṇī, dubbaṇṇinī naggayinī palāyinī;
kalahāni.translation_2: It brings pride, arrogance, quarrels, and calumny; it is ugly, naked, and makes one flee.

pesuṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form used of a bad quality or of one who slanders; in the verse it describes a state (pride, arrogance, quarrels, slander). Could also be treated as a feminine noun "slander".
pesuṇī.example_2: 44. Mānātimānā kalahāni pesuṇī, dubbaṇṇinī naggayinī palāyinī;
pesuṇī.translation_2: It brings pride, arrogance, quarrels, and calumny; it is ugly, naked, and makes one flee.

dubbaṇṇinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form of dubbaṇṇin used in this verse of the Mānatthaddha-jātaka; nominative singular in the text.
dubbaṇṇinī.example_2: 44. Mānātimānā kalahāni pesuṇī, dubbaṇṇinī naggayinī palāyinī;
dubbaṇṇinī.translation_2: It brings pride, arrogance, quarrels, and calumny; it is ugly, naked, and makes one flee.

naggayinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A descriptive feminine adjective used in a list of negative epithets, possibly personifying a woman lacking clothes or shamelessness.  Nom. sg. of an ī-stem; nominative singular in the text.
naggayinī.example_2: 44. Mānātimānā kalahāni pesuṇī, dubbaṇṇinī naggayinī palāyinī;
naggayinī.translation_2: It brings pride, arrogance, quarrels, and calumny; it is ugly, naked, and makes one flee.

niketo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text niketо is nominative singular, co-ordinating with gatī in the phrase gatī niketo. Sometimes written niketо.
niketo.example_2: Corāna dhuttāna gatī niketo, tassā puṇṇaṃ kumbhamimaṃ kiṇātha.
niketo.translation_2: It is the path and home of thieves and scoundrels; buy this jar filled with that!

ucchedanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in a Jātaka verse as a feminine adjective agreeing with an implied noun, describing a thing that ruins wealthy families. Scribe variants ucchedanī and ucchedanivitta are recorded for the second line.
ucchedanī.example_2: Ucchedanī vittavataṃ [ucchedanī vittagataṃ (syā.), ucchedanivittagataṃ (ka.)] kulānaṃ, tassā puṇṇaṃ kumbhamimaṃ kiṇātha.
ucchedanī.translation_2: this is the destruction of wealthy families; buy this jar filled with that!

ucchedanivittagataṃ.meaning_2: gone to the destruction of wealth; come to ruin of riches
ucchedanivittagataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of ucchedanī vittagataṃ; accusative singular agreeing with kumbhaṃ. The second element may also be analysed as vitta + gata, 'gone to (one's) wealth'.
ucchedanivittagataṃ.example_1: Ucchedanī vittavataṃ [ucchedanī vittagataṃ (syā.), ucchedanivittagataṃ (ka.)] kulānaṃ, tassā puṇṇaṃ kumbhamimaṃ kiṇātha.
ucchedanivittagataṃ.translation_1: this is the destruction of wealthy families; buy this jar filled with that!

nārādhayī.meaning_2: did not please; did not win over
nārādhayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + ārādhayī (aorist 3rd singular of ārādhayati). Used in Jātaka verses.
nārādhayī.example_2: 73. Kiṃ kamma kubbaṃ tava deva pāva [devapāde (sī. syā. pī.)], nārādhayī taṃ tadicchāmi sotuṃ;
nārādhayī.translation_2: “What act or word of mine, lord, caused you to be displeased, that I wish to hear?

udassaye.meaning_2: places on; sets up; establishes; installs
udassaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present causative, used in the sense 'you place (me) on the throne'. PEU suggests a possible alternative analysis as ud + √sī + si, but the causative of √as fits the sense better.
udassaye.example_2: Yamajja rajjamhi udassaye tuvaṃ, rajjampi niccheyyaṃ tayā vināhaṃ.
udassaye.translation_2: For today you wish to set me on the throne, yet I do not desire the kingdom without you.”

tuviyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Possessive adjective from tumha; the form is accusative singular dependent on sarāmi. The PEU suggests tuviya, but that entry appears to describe the bare stem, while the text form is tuviyaṃ.
tuviyaṃ.example_2: 74. Na kammunā vā vacasā va tāta, aparādhitohaṃ tuviyaṃ sarāmi;
tuviyaṃ.translation_2: “Dear son, I do not recall a single unkind act or word of yours.

bhidā.meaning_2: breaking; splitting; piercing; (the act of) breaking
bhidā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in the phrase bhidā rukkhasūle, possibly 'breaking (you) on a wooden stake'; the meaning is uncertain and the word may belong to a different noun or verb form. In the second sentence abhidā is probably a sandhi of abhidā or abhi + bhidā, not this word alone.
bhidā.example_2: Makarehi abhidā [makarehibbhidā (sī.), makarehi ’ bhidā (syā.), makarehi bhinnā (pī.)] nāvā, phalakenāhamaplaviṃ.
bhidā.translation_2: The ship was broken by sea monsters, and I drifted on a plank.

mājānamidhāvajeyya.meaning_2: may one not run here on account of (that) knowledge
mājānamidhāvajeyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution uncertain; possibly mā + ājānaṃ + idha + āvajeyya (āvajeti = to turn towards, run). Text and context unavailable.

gamyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative reading for gantvā in the verse (Sinhalese and Thai editions read gamyā); the sense is 'having gone (to)'. Perhaps a misreading of a participle gata.
gamyā.example_1: Mātu ca [mātucca (sī.)] hetu paraloka gantvā [gamyā (sī. syā.), gamya (pī.)], sukhena saggena ca sampayutto.
gamyā.translation_1: And for the sake of my mother, having gone to the other world, I am conjoined with the happiness of being reborn in heaven.”

gamya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text for gamyā, a past participle used absolutely (paraloka gantvā/gamyā); the meaning is 'having gone to the other world'. The reading gamya may also be analysed as an absolutive with -ya.
gamya.example_1: Mātu ca [mātucca (sī.)] hetu paraloka gantvā [gamyā (sī. syā.), gamya (pī.)], sukhena saggena ca sampayutto.
gamya.translation_1: And for the sake of my mother, having gone to the other world, I am conjoined with the happiness of being reborn in heaven.”

saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.grammar: sandhi, adj + nt + adj + pron + pr
saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.meaning_2: I am one who has understood birth and death; I have comprehended birth and death
saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of saṅkhāta, jāti, maraṇa, ahaṃ and asmi; verse, first person singular. Possibly also analysed as a compound saṅkhātajātīmaraṇa + ahaṃ + asmi.
saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.example_2: Saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi, yatheva me idha tathā parattha.
saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.translation_2: I have understood birth and death; as it is for me here, so it is in the next world.”

sandīpayitvā.meaning_2: having kindled; having lit; having made bright; having shown clearly
sandīpayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative sandīpeti (saṃ + √dīp, *e). The text's sandīpayitvā shows the causative vowel -aya- before -tvā. The gloss 'having kindled' fits the fire in the second sentence; 'having shown clearly' also fits the PEU. If a text variant sandīpetvā exists, it is the same word.
sandīpayitvā.example_2: Sandīpayitvā paṭivedayittha, ādīpito dāni mahāyamaggi [mayā yakkhamaggi (ka.)].
sandīpayitvā.translation_2: Having kindled it, he announced, ‘The great fire is now lit.’

kampilla.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of kapila, a city name, in these Jātaka verses; the text has kampilla with kapila as the variant. Appears in the locative and with the accusative ending -am contraction in the second line. Possible sandhi with the following word.
kampilla.example_1: Evaṃ tuvaṃ porisādā pamutto, viroca kapile [kampilla (sī. pī.), kapille (syā.)] mahānubhāva;
kampilla.translation_1: So you, released from the ogre, shine in Kampilla, great one;
kampilla.example_2: Anuññāto sotthi sukhī arogo, paccāgamā [paccāga (pī.)] kapilamalīnasattā [kampilla ’ malīnasatto (sī. pī.), kapila ’ malīnasattā (ka.)].
kampilla.translation_2: Given permission, in safety, happy and healthy, returned to Kampilla.”

kampillamalīnasatto.meaning_2: whose mind is stained by (thoughts of) the kampilla tree; with heart defiled by kampilla
kampillamalīnasatto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of kampilla (a tree, possibly Premna serratifolia), malīna (stained, tainted) and satta (being; mind). Nominative singular in the text; exact sense uncertain.

jayadisajātakaṃ.meaning_2: Jayaddisa Jātaka; the birth story of King Jayaddisa
jayadisajātakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third Jātaka in the Book of the Nines. The text reads jayadisa° (with one d, a variant); accusative singular in the sentence, as a title citation.

paṇḍūsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is a vocative used in address to a woman ('paṇḍūsi varavaṇṇini'). The analysis as a compound with si is uncertain; possibly a variant of paṇḍu or a sandhi form. The PEU entries paṇḍaka and paṇḍara are not direct matches.
paṇḍūsi.translation_2: “Why do you grieve, O slender one, so pale, O fair-complexioned one?

poraṃ.meaning_2: formerly; in the past; of old
poraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text prints poraṃ but the variant reading is puraṃ; taken here as an adverb meaning 'formerly', qualifying nigrodharājaṃ. Could also be puraṃ (ind, prep) 'before; in front of'.
poraṃ.example_1: Atha dakkhasī meghasamānavaṇṇaṃ, nigrodharājaṃ atha sahassapādaṃ [poraṃ (ka.)].
poraṃ.translation_1: Then you will see a cloud-colored one, the king of banyans, with a thousand shoots.”

bhimūla.meaning_2: having a terrible root; with a dreadful base
bhimūla.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for tumūla in the verse; a compound of bhima (terrible, from √bhī) and mūla (root), meaning 'of terrible root/foundation'. The related entry bhimma (terrible) supports this analysis.
bhimūla.example_1: 108. Tiṭṭhanti te tumūlaṃ [tumūla (syā.), bhimūla (pī. ka.)] passasantā, kuppanti vātassapi eritassa;
bhimūla.translation_1: “They stand there breathing heavily, and they get angry even at the wind if it is stirred;

vituriya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads vituriyati; the variant noted is vituriya. The PEU suggests a derivation from tūrī but the sense here is 'traversed, crossed over' with reference to the seven mountains.
vituriya.example_1: Vituriyati [vituriya so (sī. aṭṭha.)] sattagirī brahante, suvaṇṇapassaṃ nāma giriṃ uḷāraṃ.
vituriya.translation_1: Traversed those seven mighty mountains to the lofty mountain called Golden Cliff.”

olokayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in -ī (cf. abhinīharī); the simplex is oloketi, olokayati. In the verse it describes looking at the foot of the mountain.
olokayī.example_2: 115. Āruyha selaṃ bhavanaṃ kinnarānaṃ, olokayī pabbatapādamūlaṃ;
olokayī.translation_2: “Climbing the mountain, the abode of the kinnaras, he looked at the foot of the mountain;

samappayī.meaning_2: causes to attain; brings to; shoots; hits; strikes (with)
samappayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the verse (samappayī) with the same form as the present; the causative of samāpajjati, here 'struck, hit (with an arrow)'. Occurs twice in the same verse.
samappayī.translation_2: Struck the elephant, who had come by, with a poisoned arrow, a doer of evil deeds.”

adisva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of na passati (√dis 1). The text has the variant adisva (sī. pī.), a shortened form of adisvāna for the metre.
adisva.example_1: Adisvāna [adisva (sī. pī.)] posaṃ gajapaccamittaṃ, paccāgamuṃ yena so nāgarājā.
adisva.translation_1: Not seeing the man, the enemy of the elephant, they returned to where that king of snake-gods was.”

aphāli.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist of phāleti, with privative prefix na > a; refers to the heart bursting. 3rd singular.
aphāli.example_2: Tattheva tassā hadayaṃ aphāli, teneva sā kālamakāsi bālā.
aphāli.translation_2: Right there her heart broke; because of that, the foolish one died.”

ucaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text ucaṃ is a sandhi shortening of uccaṃ (accusative singular); the printed text gives uccāvacaṃ as the reading, a compound of ucca + avaca meaning 'high and low; mixed'. Here it describes conduct.
ucaṃ.example_1: 136. Anāvasūraṃ cirarattasaṃsitaṃ, uccāvacaṃ [ucaṃ nīcaṃ (sī. syā. pī.)] caritamidaṃ purāṇaṃ;
ucaṃ.translation_1: “This is the ancient, long-drawn-out, mixed, and varied conduct;

svādhippāgā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of su + ādhippāgā (or su + adhippāya in some analyses); in the Jātaka verses it occurs with bhāradvājo, possibly meaning 'Bharadvāja of good intention' if taken as a compound rather than sandhi. Text varies; see v.l. bhadrakārassa santikaṃ.
svādhippāgā.translation_2: 144. Bharadvaja went to the presence of Vidhura;

parīsati.meaning_2: in the assembly; in the presence of
parīsati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of parisati, locative of parisā, used adverbially. Sya. reads parisati.
parīsati.example_1: Tamaddasa mahābrahmā, nisinnaṃ samhi vesmani [parisati (syā.), parīsati (pī.)].
parīsati.translation_1: He saw the great brahmin sitting in his house.

atevaññehi.meaning_2: beyond others; surpassing others; excelling others
atevaññehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ati + eva + aññehi; ati here has the sense 'beyond, surpassing'. Instrumental plural agreeing with māsehi; the spelling with single t is metrical.
atevaññehi.translation_2: Excels other months, and shines with tree flowers.

nissīve.meaning_2: at midnight; in the middle of the night
nissīve.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant spelling of nisīthe (Sinhalese edition); locative of nisītha (midnight). An indeclinable adverb in this context.
nissīve.example_1: Nisīthe [nissīve (syā.), nisive (ka.)] pabbataggasmiṃ, pahūtedho [bahutejo (syā. ka.)] virocati.
nissīve.translation_1: At midnight on a mountain peak, radiates with abundant fuel.

nisive.meaning_2: at midnight; in the middle of the night
nisive.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of nisīthe (locative of nisītha, 'midnight'); the commentary form nissīve supports the same meaning. Treated here as an indeclinable adverb of time; alternatively a locative singular of a masc nisiva.
nisive.example_1: Nisīthe [nissīve (syā.), nisive (ka.)] pabbataggasmiṃ, pahūtedho [bahutejo (syā. ka.)] virocati.
nisive.translation_1: At midnight on a mountain peak, radiates with abundant fuel.

bahīpure.meaning_2: outside and inside; in the outer and inner parts (of the city); at the outskirts and within
bahīpure.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative-style adverb from bahi (outside) + pure (in front, before, inside); used of the outskirts of the city in the Jātaka verse.
bahīpure.translation_2: He saw the great brahmin playing in the outskirts of the city.

byamhito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used as an adjective. In the text nominative singular in byamhito and byamhito rājā. The PEU suggests byamhita can also mean 'surprised; afraid'. The prefix vi- with √bham ('to turn, revolve, buzz') gives the sense of agitation or alarm. The form looks irregular; the insertion of -mhi- is obscure, and a possible reading is byāmhita, pp of byāmihati. Here treated as a pp in -ita from a denominative or causative base.

duddasī.meaning_2: ugly; unsightly; difficult to look at
duddasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An adjective in -in (nom. sg. duddasī), not the verb dassati. Occurs in a list of insults. Literally 'of bad appearance'.
duddasī.translation_2: 184. “You are ugly, shapeless, unsightly, and fearful to behold;

māruyha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (Sinhalese and Syāma editions) for rukkhamārūhiṃ in the text; equivalent to āruyha with mā (prohibitive?) or sandhi; the sentence gives 'climbed the tree'.
māruyha.example_1: Atitto rukkhamārūhiṃ [māruyha (sī. syā.)], tattha hessāmi āsito.
māruyha.translation_1: Unsatisfied, I climbed the tree, thinking, ‘I will be satisfied there.’

samabhajjisaṃ.meaning_2: was not crushed; went to ruin; was ruined
samabhajjisaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular. The alternative reading samapajjisaṃ suggests confusion with √pad; the commentary (pī.) reading samabhajjisaṃ is taken as genuine.
samabhajjisaṃ.example_1: 193. Yasmā ca vāri gambhīraṃ, tasmā na samapajjisaṃ [samapajjasiṃ (sī.), samabhajjisaṃ (pī.)];
samabhajjisaṃ.translation_1: 193. “Because the water was deep, I was not crushed;

parittātuna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant spelling of parittāyitvā, absolutive of parittāyati (from pari + √tā 1). The commentary's alternate reading parittātuna is given in the text; the -una ending is unusual for an absolutive and may be metrical or scribal.
parittātuna.example_1: 204. Evaṃ me parittātūna [parittātuna (ka.)], passupi so muhuttakaṃ;
parittātuna.translation_1: 204. “After I had guarded him, he slept for a moment;

paṭilacchiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of paṭilabhati, with the ending -iṃ (cf. i aor). In the text paṭilacchiṃ is a sandhi form of paṭilabhiṃ, assimilating bh to cch. The object is diṭṭhiṃ.
paṭilacchiṃ.translation_2: Then I conceived an evil thought, unwisely.

āsiko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads āsiko, apparently a variant of asito, past participle of asati (eats) meaning 'having eaten'.
āsiko.translation_1: 206. “‘Having eaten, I will go, taking the meat as provisions;’

sannitāḷayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has sannitāḷayiṃ, the 1st person singular aorist. The PEU splits it as saṃ + ni + tāḷa + ṇaya; the ṇ is a purely grammatical insertion. Here it means 'I struck', referring to the head.
sannitāḷayiṃ.translation_2: 207. “Then, having taken a stone, I struck his head;

māyyomaṃ.meaning_2: do not this; don't do this
māyyomaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] mā + yomaṃ (yo + imaṃ) per the commentary, or mā + imaṃ; a prohibition with a demonstrative object. Cf. bhaddante in the same line. Variant reading may divide differently.
māyyomaṃ.example_2: 209. Māyyomaṃ kari bhaddante, tvañca nāmedisaṃ kari;
māyyomaṃ.translation_2: 209. “‘Do not act thus, good sir; you should not act in such a way;’

pakkhalya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive form (gerund) of pakkhalati in the sense of washing or cleansing; used with matthakaṃ ('the head'). Not found in the given root list; possibly related to √khal 3.
pakkhalya.example_2: 215. Idaṃ vatvā giricaro, rahade [ruhiraṃ (syā. ka.)] pakkhalya matthakaṃ;
pakkhalya.translation_2: 215. “Having said this, the mountain-dweller washed his head in a pool;

sampamajjitvā.meaning_2: having wiped away; having wiped clean; having wiped dry
sampamajjitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā; in the text it governs assūni ('tears'). The PEU entry reads saṃ + pa + majja + tvā.
sampamajjitvā.translation_2: Having wiped away his tears, he then climbed the mountain.

idhaddubhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text idhaddubhi is a sandhi of idha + dubbhati (variant reading idhaddubhi for idha dubbhati); the entry is given here for the first part idha. Alternative sandhi analysis: idha + adubbhi.
idhaddubhi.example_1: 223. Kuṭṭhī kilāsī bhavati, yo mittānidha dubbhati [yo mittānaṃ idhaddubhi (sī. aṭṭha.), yo mittānaṃ idha dubbhati (pī.)];
idhaddubhi.translation_1: 223. “One who is treacherous to friends here becomes a leper;

muñcesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form muñcesi appears to be a causative (or causative-like) form of muñcati, meaning 'you release' or 'you cause to be released'. The commentary glosses it with dakarakkhasā, suggesting it may also be read as an aorist or optative-like form. In the Jātaka verse, it describes releasing a water-demon.
muñcesi.translation_2: having given them in proper order, you would release the water-demon.”

chabbhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the vocative, addressed in the verse (chabbhī ... tayi padussati: 'Chabbhī, [who] bears ill-will towards you'). Exact derivation uncertain; treated as an indeclinable proper name.
chabbhī.example_2: Chabbhī tayi padussati [paduṭṭhasmiṃ (sī. syā.)], paṇḍitā atthadassinī;
chabbhī.translation_2: she who is wise and sees the goal, why do you bear ill-will toward her?

parimocayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text (§1–3), formed from the causative stem; short final -i is metrical. Alternative infinitive/absolutive-like analysis is unlikely here.

gabbhadhāriṇiṃ.meaning_2: pregnant woman; woman carrying a child in the womb
gabbhadhāriṇiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Spelling gabbhadhāriṇiṃ (with ṇ) in the text, variant gabbhadhāriniṃ; accusative singular, describing the mother. The PEU adds a suffix inī and root √dhar, but the compound is entered without root fields.
gabbhadhāriṇiṃ.example_1: 227. Taṃ tādisiṃ [tādisaṃ (ka.)] pāṇadadiṃ, orasaṃ gabbhadhāriniṃ [gabbhadhāriṇiṃ (sī. syā.)];
gabbhadhāriṇiṃ.translation_1: “That one who gave life, my own mother who carried me in her womb,

uppariṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of upariṃ / upari, with the p doubled for the metre (as noted in the commentary gloss ubbariṃ). Prepositional use would govern a noun in the genitive or locative.
uppariṃ.translation_1: for what fault would you give Ubbari to the water-demon?”

ubbariyāpihaṃ.meaning_2: also here in the Ubbari (verse); indeed here with Ubbarī
ubbariyāpihaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Uncertain, possibly corrupted verse. Probably sandhi of ubbariyā (locative of Ubbarī) + api + ahaṃ, or ubbariyā + pi + ahaṃ. Ubbarī appears to be a woman's name. The following ayye is a separate word.
ubbariyāpihaṃ.translation_2: Also, when I am in private with Ubbari, noble lady,

ummīlitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form in the text is the absolutive of ummīleti, causative of √mīl ('close the eyes'), used of opening the eyes and looking (udikkhati). The related PEU entry gives ummīlitvā = 'having opened'. Possible alternates: ummīlayati/ummīleti.
ummīlitvā.translation_2: “Even in the assembly, noble lady, he opens his eyes and looks at me;

pallittho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading pallittho for pallatthito. Appears in a tetrameter verse, so the form may be metrically shaped. Parsed as a past participle meaning 'trapped; caught', in the nominative singular; comparison with pallatthito suggests pallittho may stand for pallatthito.
pallittho.example_1: Dosā bhayā athavā rāgarattā [rāgaratto (sī. syā. pī.)], pallatthito [pallittho (pī.), pallattito (ka.)] bālo asaṃsayaṃ so.
pallittho.translation_1: Whether from hatred, fear, or because they are dyed in lust, that fool is undoubtedly trapped.

pallattito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading pallittha in some editions. Nominative singular masculine in the text, describing a fool. The root is uncertain; perhaps a by-form of √lat 'to cling' or √latt.
pallattito.example_1: Dosā bhayā athavā rāgarattā [rāgaratto (sī. syā. pī.)], pallatthito [pallittho (pī.), pallattito (ka.)] bālo asaṃsayaṃ so.
pallattito.translation_1: Whether from hatred, fear, or because they are dyed in lust, that fool is undoubtedly trapped.

mudīreti.meaning_2: utters; speaks out; gives voice to
mudīreti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present in the verse; the verb is used of uttering speech in assemblies.
mudīreti.example_2: 264. Tirokkhavāco asataṃ paviṭṭho, yo saṅgatīsu mudīreti vākyaṃ;
mudīreti.translation_2: One who speaks scattered words, entering into the company of the wicked, who utters such speech in gatherings;

asmiṃdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular of ima ('asmiṃ') joined with idha ('here'), so 'here in this'. Variant reading 'asmiṃ idha'. The whole phrase asmiṃdha loke = 'in this world here'.
asmiṃdha.example_1: 266. Ko nīdha tiṇṇaṃ garahaṃ upeti, asmiṃdha loke pāṇabhū nāgarāja;
asmiṃdha.translation_1: Who in this world, O snake-king, now incurs blame among these three people?

paṇḍarakaggahīto.meaning_2: seized by Paṇḍaraka; caught by Paṇḍaraka
paṇḍarakaggahīto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the text (paṇḍarakaggahīto). Paṇḍaraka is the name of the nāga king in this Jātaka verse.
paṇḍarakaggahīto.example_2: Samaṇo supaṇṇo atha vā tvameva, kiṃ kāraṇā paṇḍarakaggahīto.
paṇḍarakaggahīto.translation_2: Is it the samaṇa, the Garuda, or you yourself? For what reason were you seized, Paṇḍara?

alabbhamabyāharatī.meaning_2: speaks of the unattainable; speaks of what cannot be obtained
alabbhamabyāharatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound verb (alabbhaṃ + abyāharati); the text form -tī is metrical for -ti. 3rd singular.
alabbhamabyāharatī.example_2: Saccena dhammena dhitiyā [dhiyā (sī. pī.)] damena, alabbhamabyāharatī naro idha.
alabbhamabyāharatī.translation_2: By truth, Dhamma, memory, and self-control, a person here speaks of the unattainable.

byavajanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural present in the text (byavajanti). The PEU splits it as vi + ava + aja + anti with the sense 'depart'. In the verse it means enemies keep far away from them.
byavajanti.example_2: Ārā amittā byavajanti tehi, āsīvisā vā riva sattusaṅghā [sattasaṅghā (sī. syā.)].
byavajanti.translation_2: Enemies keep far away from them, just as groups of enemies flee from a venomous snake.

tamhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text tamhī is tamhi (locative singular of ta) with the emphatic -ī, variant reading for tamhi; taṃ refers to the person addressed. Not the adjective tamba ('copper-coloured').
tamhī.example_1: Tamhi [tamhī (pī.)] nu kho vivariṃ guyhamatthaṃ, atthā ca dhammā ca apaggatamhā [apāgatamhā (sī.), apagatamhā (syā.), avāgatamhā (pī.)].
tamhī.translation_1: Did I reveal my secret to him? Both benefits and qualities have departed from there.

dijinda.meaning_2: lord of the birds; king of birds
dijinda.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative addressing the bird; an epithet of the Buddha in the Jātaka verse.
dijinda.example_2: Evampi me tvaṃ pāturahu dijinda, mātāva puttaṃ anukampamāno.
dijinda.translation_2: So have you appeared to me, O king of birds, out of compassion, like a mother to her child.

bhumyaṃ.meaning_2: on the ground; on the earth
bhumyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular of bhumī (the usual spelling is bhūmi); the text has the shortened bhumya- form before the ending -aṃ. Locative singular in the verse.
bhumyaṃ.example_2: 284. Icceva vākyaṃ visajjī supaṇṇo, bhumyaṃ patiṭṭhāya dijo dujivhaṃ;
bhumyaṃ.translation_2: Thus the Garuda spoke this word, having set the double-tongued bird on the ground;

kādambiyaṃ.meaning_2: Karambiya; Kādambiya; name of a place
kādambiyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of karambiya in the Jātaka verse; accusative singular in the text, an ablative/locative-style derivation from kādamba meaning 'belonging to the Kadamba tree region'. Possibly an adjective or a proper name of a place.
kādambiyaṃ.example_1: Upāgamuṃ karampiyaṃ [kādambiyaṃ (sī.), kārambiyaṃ (pī.)] acelaṃ, missībhūtā assavāhāva nāgā.
kādambiyaṃ.translation_1: Approached the naked ascetic at Karambiya, united like bull elephants yoked together.

kārambiyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternate reading of kādambiya in the text. It is a place name, here in the accusative singular after upāgamuṃ. The compound may be kāra + mbiya, but the analysis is uncertain.
kārambiyaṃ.example_1: Upāgamuṃ karampiyaṃ [kādambiyaṃ (sī.), kārambiyaṃ (pī.)] acelaṃ, missībhūtā assavāhāva nāgā.
kārambiyaṃ.translation_1: Approached the naked ascetic at Karambiya, united like bull elephants yoked together.

dūbhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading dubbhī. Nominative singular describing a person who betrays; in the text it qualifies the backbiter (pisuṇo).
dūbhī.example_1: 295. Aduṭṭhassa tuvaṃ dubbhi, dubbhī [dūbhi, dūbhī (pī.)] ca pisuṇo casi;
dūbhī.translation_1: ‘You are treacherous to one who has no malice, and you are double-tongued and backbiting;’

saññatūra.meaning_2: with thighs held still; whose thighs are restrained; standing still with bound thighs
saññatūra.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of saṃhitūru in the verse (Sī. Pī. saññatūra; Syā. sañcitūru). The PEU analysis saññatā + ñīru seems doubtful; a compound saññata + ūra (thigh) fits the 'standing still and trembling' context better. Vocative singular in the text.
saññatūra.example_1: 297. Kā vedhamānā girikandarāyaṃ, ekā tuvaṃ tiṭṭhasi saṃhitūru [saññatūra (sī. pī.), sañcitūru (syā.)];
saññatūra.translation_1: “Tied to the spot and trembling as in fear, who in this rocky cave is standing here?

sambulā.meaning_2: Sambulā (name of a queen; wife of a demon in the Sambulā Jātaka)
sambulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a queen in the Sambulā Jātaka. Nominative singular in the text.

sambulāhaṃ.meaning_2: 'I am Sambulā'; name of a woman; Sambulā
sambulāhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form is sambulā + ahaṃ ('I am Sambulā'); ahaṃ is treated separately. In the second occurrence, sambulā is followed by ahaṃ, which scans as sambulāhaṃ.
sambulāhaṃ.example_2: Abhivādemi taṃ bhante [bhaddante (sī. syā.)], sambulāhaṃ namatthu te.
sambulāhaṃ.translation_2: I salute you, good sir; I am Sambulā; let there be a greeting for you.”

sambule.meaning_2: name of a queen; name of a character in the Sambula Jātaka
sambule.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the text, addressing the queen Sambulā. The reading sambule is likely a vocative of sambulā or an alternate form; PEU lists sambula as a queen's name.

sambulaṃ.meaning_2: name of a queen; Sambulā (wife of king Sotthisena, known from the Sambulā story)
sambulaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name. Accusative singular sambulaṃ in the text, object of aggahī (aorist of gaṇhāti), 'seized Sambulā by the arm'.
sambulaṃ.example_2: Vane nāthaṃ apassantiṃ, sambulaṃ aggahī bhuje.
sambulaṃ.translation_2: Seized Sambulā by the arm, as she looked for her lord in the forest.”

paḷinaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Rare word, found in Jātaka verse; variant readings phalina and niḍḍa. Neuter accusative singular in the text, in the simile of a bird returning to its nest or shelter. Perhaps a dialectal form of palina or related to palāla.
paḷinaṃ.example_2: Nīḷaṃ [niḍḍaṃ (syā. ka.)] paḷinaṃ sakuṇīva [phalinasakuṇīva (sī. syā. pī.)], gatasiṅgaṃva ālayaṃ.
paḷinaṃ.translation_2: Like a bird returning to its nest, like one who has gone to her refuge.”

latāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is plural, latāni, though latā is feminine and this would normally be latāyo ; possibly a metrical form or a masculine/neuter reanalysis. See also latā as a tree branch or reed.
latāni.example_2: 316. Tiṇā [tiṇa (pī.)] latāni osadhyo, pabbatāni vanāni ca;
latāni.translation_2: The grasses, the creepers, the medicinal plants, the mountains and the forests;

indīvarīsāmaṃ.meaning_2: dark as a blue lotus; resembling a blue water lily
indīvarīsāmaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of indīvarī + sāma (fem ending -ī before consonant). Used of the night in the verse; accusative singular agreeing with rattiṃ in the following line.
indīvarīsāmaṃ.translation_2: I salute the night, dark as a blue lotus, bedecked with stars;

vimānaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular in the verse (sammānaye ... na ca maṃ vimānaye), expressing 'would honour ... would not despise'. The root √mān is not in the given list.
vimānaye.example_1: sammānaye maṃ na ca maṃ vimānaye,
vimānaye.example_2: Sammānaye maṃ na ca maṃ vimānaye, itopi me tāta tato varaṃ siyā.
vimānaye.translation_2: He would honor me and not despise me; that would be better for me, dear, than this.”

ābajjha.meaning_2: fit to be tied up; to be bound; captive; (variant reading of avajjha)
ābajjha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A variant reading (pī) for avajjha in the verse; here it contrasts with appiyā ('unloved'), so the sense is 'to be bound, captive'. Indeclinable in form; some editions read avajjha ('not to be killed; inviolable').
ābajjha.example_1: Sabbaṅgupetā [pañcaṅgupetā (sī. syā. pī.)] patino ca appiyā, abajjha [avajjha (syā.), ābajjha (pī.)] tassā maraṇaṃ tato varaṃ.
ābajjha.translation_1: Possessed of all parts, but unloved by her husband, death is better than that.”

sambulāya.meaning_2: Sambulā; name of a queen (wife of King Maddava in the Sambulā Jātaka)
sambulāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name; dative case in the text (janinda dhammaṃ cara sambulāya = practise the Dhamma towards Sambulā). Could be read as dative/genitive of the ā-stem. The PEU treats sambula as an alternate form.
sambulāya.example_2: Hitā ca te sīlavatī ca bhariyā, janinda dhammaṃ cara sambulāya.
sambulāya.translation_2: Your wife is helpful and virtuous; O King, practice the Dhamma toward Sambulā.”

hiraññanidhāniyā.meaning_2: treasure of gold; gold and treasure
hiraññanidhāniyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads hiraññanidhāniyā, variant of hiraññanidhiyā (nominative hiraññanidhi), compound of hirañña + nidhi. The sense is 'gold and treasure' or 'treasure of gold' in a list of wealth. Extraction is uncertain.
hiraññanidhāniyā.example_1: 337. Na te puttā bhavissanti, na hiraññaṃ na dhāniyaṃ [na hiraññanidhāniyā (ka.)];
hiraññanidhāniyā.translation_1: 337. There will be no sons for you, no silver, no grain;

dubbalacakkhūsi.meaning_2: weak-eyed; with weak sight; having blurred vision
dubbalacakkhūsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in -si (dubbalacakkhūsi) with elision of the final vowel of the stem; the suffix -ka in the PEU entries is secondary. Compound of dubbala and cakkhu. Used of an old man in the verse.
dubbalacakkhūsi.example_2: 344. Jiṇṇo dubbalacakkhūsi, na rūpaṃ sādhu passasi;
dubbalacakkhūsi.translation_2: 344. You are old and weak-sighted, you do not see the form well;

maggheyya.meaning_2: would seek; should seek; would search for
maggheyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular, possibly with an added -h- (maggheyya for maggeyya). The variant reading maggeyya is perhaps preferable. In the sentence: 'yaṃ taṃ maggheyya kaṇṭako' = 'a thorn that might pierce you'.
maggheyya.example_1: Kiṃ tattha brahmadattassa, yaṃ taṃ maggeyya [maggheyya (pī.)] kaṇṭako [kaṇḍako (sī. syā. pī.)].
maggheyya.translation_1: What is it to Brahmadatta that a thorn should pierce you there?

tuṇḍiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it is nominative plural (tuṇḍiyā) and stands for robbers who plunder by day, in contrast with corā by night. The PEU takes tuṇḍiya as tuṇḍa + ika with a y-suffix, glossed as a violent robber. The final -ā is probably a Nominative plural in -ā, though it could be read as a singular of the -ā stem; the plural is preferred because the verb khādanti is plural.
tuṇḍiyā.example_2: 346. Rattiñhi [rattiñca (sī.)] corā khādanti, divā khādanti tuṇḍiyā;
tuṇḍiyā.translation_2: 346. By night robbers devour them, by day those who harass devour them;

nillenakāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural form nillenakāni in the text. Possibly a compound with līna (hidden), but the exact derivation is uncertain.
nillenakāni.translation_2: They make hiding places, having brought thorns into the forest.

aṭanaka.meaning_2: running about; restless; of a wandering nature; prone to stray
aṭanaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used of a cow in Jātaka 361; the commentary glosses akaṭanā (not milked?) as variant. The form is nominative singular feminine modifying gāvī.}
aṭanaka.example_1: 361. Caṇḍā aṭanakā [aṭanaka (pī.), akaṭanā (ka.)] gāvī, yaṃ pure na duhāmase;
aṭanaka.translation_1: 361. The cow, which formerly we did not milk, is foolish and prone to run away;

viputto.meaning_2: deprived of a son; bereft of sons; separated from his son
viputto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse viputto vippasukkhatu, viputto is nominative singular agreeing with pañcālo, meaning 'bereft of his son(s)'. Sometimes analysed as vi + putta; the second part vippasukkhatu is a separate verb.
viputto.translation_2: 362. May Pañcāla be thus crying, deprived of his sons and suffering;

viputtā.meaning_2: deprived of a calf; separated from her calf; bereft of a son
viputtā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text viputtā is nominative singular feminine, agreeing with gāvī (cow), meaning 'without her calf'. Literally vi (without) + putta (son/child), but used here for a calf. Could also be read as masculine plural of viputta in other contexts.
viputtā.translation_2: Just as this wretched cow runs about, deprived of her calf.

khīrapā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a child still drinking milk. In the verse khīrapā modifies pajā, "the people, [like] sucklings"; the form is nominative singular of the compound adjective.
khīrapā.example_2: Kathaṃ no asikosatthā, khīrapā haññate pajā.
khīrapā.translation_2: How is it that the people, sword-struck, are killed while milking?

jayaddisa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The hero of the Jayaddisa Jātaka, cited in the verse as a famous name.
jayaddisa.example_2: Kiṃchanda kumbha jayaddisa chaddanta, atha paṇḍitasambhava sirakapi;
jayaddisa.translation_2: Kiṃchanda, Kumbha, Jayaddisa, Chaddanta, and Paṇḍitasambhava, Sirakapi;

sambula.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name; part of the compound sambulatindukadevasuta. The text's sambula is the first member, not a nominative in -a.
sambula.translation_2: Dakarakkhasa, Paṇḍaranāgavara, and Sambula, the Tindukadeva story.

mappamajjato.meaning_2: not negligent; who is not heedless
mappamajjato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + pamajjato, genitive singular of pamajjanta, present participle of pamajjati (√majj, be negligent). Alternative sandhi of na + appamajjato. The text reads anutiṭṭhanti devatā.
mappamajjato.translation_1: For one who works and is not negligent, the devas stand by to assist.
